doc.title: Jackie Cain and Roy Kral interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998

chapter: Time and Love and later records
title: Listening to their old records and Cy Coleman
summary: They seldom listen to their records; it led to re-recording 'East of Suez' and a Berlin DJ's interest in the Cy Coleman album.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Now do you listen to yourself, your recordings?
Not after we once do them.
Very seldom. We’ll hear them, we’ll go to someone’s house and they’ll play something of ours—
They think they’re doing us a favor when we’d come over to a party or something, they’re playing your records.

In fact, that’s what led us back to “East of Suez.” Because we went into this place and they were playing “East of Suez.” I said God, that sounds great, let’s do that one again. So we put it in the right key and we did it again.

But actually when you walk into somebody’s house and they think that you’ll enjoy it, you know, and it’s really nice that they have them and that they play them, but all of a sudden you don’t hear any conversation, you’re listening to it.
Yeah, why did I do that, and there’s always something that’s a little funny that you could have done better, and you kind of re-live the day that you did it. It throws you right back there.
I’m trying to think the other day, a few days ago, I said let’s put that in again, oh, Cy Coleman’s “My City.”
And I haven’t heard it in 15 years since we recorded it. And we never wanted to do it but I think we might go back to that one.

Like last May we met this friend from Berlin, we’d never met him before, and Susanna McCorkle introduced us to him. And he’s a D.J. and has his own radio show over there, and plays a lot of theater music and plays jazz because he personally likes jazz. And he’s on all the time. And so he had been a fan of ours and had many of our records but had never met us, so we met him. And so now he said could I come out and do an interview with you. So he came out and we started talking about these different things. Like he wanted to do a whole Cy Coleman program. So we hadn’t heard it since we did it really. And so I said well I think I have one, I’ll find one for you, so I found him a tape, and then I thought gee I’d better listen to what the heck is on that thing, I don’t remember all the songs we did. And we listened to it and said gee that sounds pretty good. Because when you listen to things that are older you forget, because you don’t do all of them, sometimes you’ll take one two from this album and one or two from another one and so on and so forth. You always like your current things the best because they’re the freshest.
